teaching_point: Small pigmented dermatofibroma on the upper arm. It is brown in darker skin types and slowly grows from a 'speck'.

teaching_point: Firm papule with a darker peripheral rim and paler centre. This 'fried-egg' look is typical, and the dimple sign confirms it.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Dermatofibroma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/dermatofibroma

teaching_point: Pink-brown firm papule. DF often itches occasionally and is usually left alone.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Dermatofibroma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/dermatofibroma

teaching_point: Dermoscopy of a pigmented DF: delicate peripheral network with a central paler zone.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Dermatoscopy of dermatofibroma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/dermatofibroma-images

teaching_point: Bland structureless pigmentation on dermoscopy. Atypical patterns overlap with melanoma, so biopsy or refer if there is uncertainty or change.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Dermoscopy. Bland, structureless pigmentation: dermatofibroma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/dermatofibroma-images

teaching_point: Tender crusted nodule on the helical rim. Exquisite tenderness on light squeezing is the bedside test; ask about sleeping side (post-stroke immobility).
dermnet_caption: Image provided by Dr Trevor Evans
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Image provided by Dr Trevor Evans (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/chondrodermatitis-nodularis

teaching_point: CNH with surrounding erythema on the upper helix. First-line treatment is pressure relief (hollowed pillow or ear-protector device).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Chondrodermatitis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/chondrodermatitis-nodularis

teaching_point: CNH on the antihelix (women more often). A scaly nodule like this can mimic SCC or BCC, so refer if it is atypical, growing or not settling with pressure relief.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Chondrodermatitis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/chondrodermatitis-nodularis

teaching_point: Gouty tophi on the ear: chalky white-yellow nodules, often multiple and less tender. Ask about joint gout; urate level.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Gouty tophi (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/gout

teaching_point: Keratoacanthoma: rapidly growing dome with a keratin-filled crater over weeks. Treat as SCC (suspected cancer pathway referral, NG12 1.7.4).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Keratoacanthoma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/keratoacanthoma

teaching_point: Multiple stuck-on SKs on the back of an older adult. Many similar lesions are reassuring, but a single 'ugly duckling' is not.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Seborrhoeic keratosis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/seborrhoeic-keratosis-images

teaching_point: Dark, raised SKs on the trunk. A black, enlarging lesion that a partner has noticed is exactly when a non-expert should not reassure without dermoscopy.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Seborrhoeic keratosis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/seborrhoeic-keratosis-images

teaching_point: Early flat tan SK. It can look like a solar lentigo or early melanoma, so check for sharp edges and surface keratin.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Seborrhoeic keratosis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/seborrhoeic-keratosis

teaching_point: Pigmented facial SK. On sun-damaged face, lentigo maligna is the key DDx, so refer if there is irregular pigment or change.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Seborrhoeic keratosis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/seborrhoeic-keratosis

teaching_point: Classic waxy 'stuck-on' papule with a warty surface. This is the reassuring look.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Seborrhoeic keratosis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/seborrhoeic-keratosis

teaching_point: Irritated SK: red, inflamed and possibly crusted. It looks worrying and can mimic SCC or amelanotic melanoma; if in doubt refer, as histology may be needed.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Irritated seborrhoeic keratosis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/seborrhoeic-keratosis

teaching_point: Many SKs on the trunk. A sudden eruption of numerous SKs (sign of Leser–Trélat) is a rare paraneoplastic sign; ask about weight loss and GI symptoms.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Seborrhoeic keratoses (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/sign-of-leser-trelat

teaching_point: Dermoscopy: white milia-like cysts and comedo-like openings.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Seborrhoeic keratosis dermoscopy (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/seborrhoeic-keratosis-dermoscopy-images

teaching_point: Dermoscopy: 'brain-like' fissures and ridges (cerebriform pattern).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Seborrhoeic keratosis dermoscopy (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/seborrhoeic-keratosis-dermoscopy-images

teaching_point: Dermoscopy: multiple comedo-like openings on a light-brown background.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Seborrhoeic keratosis dermoscopy (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/seborrhoeic-keratosis-dermoscopy-images

teaching_point: Dermoscopy: sharply demarcated, moth-eaten border. Abrupt edges favour SK over melanoma.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Seborrhoeic keratosis dermoscopy (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/seborrhoeic-keratosis-dermoscopy-images

teaching_point: Dermoscopy: crowded orange-yellow cysts/openings. Hairpin or comma vessels may be seen in thicker SKs.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Dermoscopy of seborrhoeic keratosis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/seborrhoeic-keratosis-dermoscopy-images

teaching_point: Multicoloured SK on dermoscopy. Colour variety alone can be benign, but this is why dermoscopy without training must not be used to reassure.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Multiple colours (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/seborrhoeic-keratosis-dermoscopy-images

teaching_point: Clear cell acanthoma: solitary moist red dome-shaped papule, usually on the lower leg of a middle-aged or older adult.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Clear cell acanthoma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/clear-cell-acanthoma

teaching_point: CCA with a scaly collarette on a hairy leg. DDx: pyogenic granuloma, amelanotic melanoma, Bowen's disease. Usually excised for diagnosis.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Clear cell acanthoma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/clear-cell-acanthoma

teaching_point: Close-up of CCA showing dotted and glomerular vessels arranged in a 'string of pearls' (necklace) pattern, the dermoscopic hallmark.
